articles.title: Angel Reese switches things up with a new hairstyle as her bangs steal the spotlight
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star knows how to keep her style fresh, and even a small change is enough to get fans talking
articles.summary: The WNBA star knows how to keep her style fresh, and even a small change is enough to get fans talking
articles.body:
A ngel Reese knows how to keep things fresh and find new ways to stand out. The basketball star has become a fashion icon, making it a priority to switch things up and stay ahead of trends. Even during the offseason, Reese knows how to draw attention to herself, and her latest hairstyle change was no exception. Although it was a subtle detail, it was one fans had not seen from her before.

Reese is no stranger to changing her appearance whenever she feels like it. Throughout the years, she has experimented with several hairstyles, including a bob, pink hair, braids, straightened looks and natural curls. Now, she has decided to add another option to the list by bringing bangs into the mix.

A new detail makes all the difference

Bangs never really go out of style, and Reese found a way to make them her own. She showed off her latest look through her Instagram Stories, revealing that the fringe is now part of her hairstyle rotation. The look she chose to introduce the change also complemented the new haircut, giving her a more mysterious and sensual appearance while taking the hairstyle to another level.

Reese is making the most of her offseason

The Atlanta Dream star had previously announced that Florida would be her home during the offseason . As well as wanting to be closer to her boyfriend, Orlando Magic player Wendell Carter Jr., Reese explained that she planned to dedicate this period to herself and continue working on her personal brand away from the spotlight.

Her latest hairstyle change fits into that approach, as Reese continues to explore different ways to express herself outside the basketball court. With several looks already behind her, the new bangs add another style to a collection that keeps evolving.

articles.title: Lexie Hull got married and Caitlin Clark surprised in a photo with a detail worth nearly $1,000
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star accompanied her teammate to her wedding in Mexico, but one of the celebration photos sparked fans' curiosity over a particular detail of her look.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star accompanied her teammate to her wedding in Mexico, but one of the celebration photos sparked fans' curiosity over a particular detail of her look.
articles.body:
Lexie Hull and Will Matthiessen celebrated their wedding last Saturday, November 21, in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico.

The ceremony brought together some 120 guests and was attended by several people close to the Indiana Fever player, including Caitlin Clark, who ended up drawing the attention of followers in the event photos.

People magazine shared ten images from the celebration, and one of them quickly began circulating among fans. In the photo, Clark appears smiling and makes an OK gesture with both hands toward the camera. But there was another detail that sparked comments: the dress she chose to accompany her teammate on such a special occasion.

Caitlin Clark's dress that caught fans' attention

After the photographs circulated, some fans identified the garment worn by the Indiana Fever star. It is the Cassidy Knit Gown model by the brand Cult Gaia, in the Coastal color, priced at around $998 .

The design is knitted, sleeveless, and features braided details and an open back. Thus, one of the wedding images also ended up becoming an opportunity for fans to notice Clark's look and find out how much it cost.

This was Lexie Hull's wedding in Mexico

The celebration took place at Sunset Monalisa, in Cabo San Lucas, with about 120 guests. The couple exchanged handwritten vows and chose an aesthetic that Hull defined as “elevated coastal”, a combination of romance, neutral tones, and ocean-inspired details.

We are looking for a sophisticated coastal aesthetic that conveys romance, timelessness, and naturalness. We love pure whites and neutral tones, with subtle ocean-inspired colors and organic textures

The bride also described the atmosphere they were looking for for the celebration: “The overall atmosphere is a mix between a coastal-style magazine and an intimate, very fun celebration with our favorite people”. For the occasion, Hull wore a dress by the brand KYHA.

Caitlin Clark wasn't the only Indiana Fever teammate invited

Another Indiana Fever member who was present was Sophie Cunningham. Her attendance was also confirmed, although she has not appeared in any yet.

Clark, meanwhile, was captured in one of the images that sparked the most comments among fans. Her expression in front of the camera and the nearly $1,000 dress made her presence become one of the most talked-about details of Lexie Hul l's wedding.

articles.title: WNBA boyfriend mystery solved: Who is Kelsey Plum’s new man?
articles.standfirst: One photo was enough to get WNBA fans talking about the basketball star's personal life
articles.summary: One photo was enough to get WNBA fans talking about the basketball star's personal life
articles.body:
K elsey Plum has given followers a rare glimpse into her offseason after spending several weeks away from social media . The Phoenix Mercury guard returned to Instagram with a collection of photographs documenting what she has been doing away from the basketball court , offering a look at some of her recent activities and personal moments.

The post quickly attracted attention, particularly because it came after a relatively quiet period for the five-time All-Star. While most of the pictures showed different aspects of her life, one image stood out and prompted plenty of curiosity among her followers.

Kelsey Plum's Instagram post raises questions about her love life

Among the photographs was a beachside moment featuring Plum alongside an unidentified man. The basketball player had her arm around him as they looked toward the water, but his back was turned to the camera, making it impossible to establish his identity.

The image immediately fueled speculation that Plum might be introducing a new romantic partner. However, she has not shared his name or provided any details about their relationship, meaning fans are still waiting for confirmation about who the man is.

A new chapter after her divorce from Darren Waller

The attention surrounding the photograph also brings back memories of Plum's previous relationship with former NFL tight end Darren Waller . The two married in 2023, but their marriage ended in 2024 after approximately one year together. Since their separation, Plum has largely kept her romantic life away from the spotlight. Her latest Instagram activity has therefore generated additional interest, although there is currently no public confirmation that the unidentified man is officially her boyfriend.

Away from her personal life, Plum is also approaching an important offseason in her basketball career . After spending seven seasons with the Las Vegas Aces, she joined the Los Angeles Sparks ahead of the 2025 campaign before being traded to the Phoenix Mercury in August 2026. The guard is now set to become an unrestricted free agent, leaving questions about her next basketball destination. For now, both her professional future and the identity of the man featured in her latest Instagram post remain topics of interest, with Plum yet to provide further details.

Sophie Cunningham has sparked a debate among conservative Christian figures after appearing topless in Maxim magazine, drawing criticism from individuals who previously praised the WNBA star for her outspoken views on women's sports and transgender athletes.

The Indiana Fever guard is on the cover of Maxim's November/December 2026 issue, photographed by Gilles Bensimon . Among the collection of images is a particularly revealing shot showing Cunningham without a top, using her long blonde hair to cover her chest.

While the photoshoot has attracted widespread attention, it's also created an unexpected disagreement among some of her supporters.

Robert P. George, a Princeton University professor and prominent conservative Catholic scholar, voiced his disappointment in a Facebook post.

According to the Christian Post, George acknowledged Cunningham's previous comments on patriotism and what he described as gender-related issues but said he could no longer support presenting her as a role model for young women.

“I can no longer, however, share the view of those who urge young women to regard her as a role model,” George wrote.

“I wouldn’t want my own daughter and granddaughters to do that. Her pornifying herself in photographs for Maxim magazine makes that impossible. I’m mystified as to why she would do such a thing.”

Evangelist Justin Peters also expressed reservations, suggesting Christian leaders should be more cautious about celebrating celebrities simply because they publicly mention their religious beliefs.

Cunningham opens up about her Maxim appearance and Christian beliefs

Interestingly, Cunningham didn't shy away from discussing her faith in the magazine's accompanying interview. She explained that her future husband would need to be Christ-centered, confident, loyal and capable of encouraging her relationship with Jesus .

“I have a very high standard for my future husband,” Cunningham said. “He’ll be someone who is Christ-centered and can lead me in my walk with Jesus.

“Someone who’s friendly, confident, and secure. Someone who is taller than me and athletic and just a good human with similar morals and values. With what I do for a living, I have to have someone who’s confident, secure, and able to kind of shoot the shit a little bit because that’s who I am. I don’t live a typical lifestyle.”

The basketball star also revealed that she'd eventually like to embrace a more traditional lifestyle, potentially settling down, getting married and having children.

“I hope one day to kind of have more of a traditional lifestyle of being in one spot, having a husband and kids and whatnot,” said Cunningham.

“But I prayed for this life, and I’m still having fun with it. But when it comes to a guy, I want someone who could push me in my faith, someone who is loyal, and someone who also loves every little piece of me.”

Cunningham also addressed the magazine collaboration on her No Hesitation podcast, explaining that her representatives initially questioned the opportunity because they associated Maxim with its previous reputation as a men's magazine.

She said their concerns changed after discovering that the publication had rebranded. Cunningham subsequently enjoyed the Indianapolis photoshoot, even joking about the expensive leather trousers she wore, which she estimated cost approximately $27,000 and required four people to help her put on.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark showed up at Penn with a surprise for Fran McCaffery’s players
articles.standfirst: Clark watched Penn beat Drexel in Philadelphia
articles.summary: Clark watched Penn beat Drexel in Philadelphia
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s visit to Penn carried a family connection and a reported gift for the team. The Indiana Fever star was at The Palestra on Tuesday to watch the Quakers beat Drexel 89-74. She also brought some of Penn coach Fran McCaffery’s players a pair of her signature Nike Caitlin 1 shoes.

Penn is coached by Fran McCaffery, the father of Clark’s boyfriend, Connor McCaffery. Caitlin and Connor both attended Iowa, giving her visit a personal tie to the Quakers beyond the game. Fran coached Iowa’s men’s team before taking over at Penn.

The Caitlin 1 shoes behind the surprise

The reported gift was the Caitlin 1 “Cave Stone,” a cream-and-brown colorway from Clark’s first signature shoe line with Nike. The retail version is listed at $140 and features details tied to Clark, including a double Swoosh and “CC” and “22” markings on the upper.

The shoes add a personal touch to Clark’s growing connection with the line. Earlier this month, Iowa’s women’s basketball team shared that she had sent the Hawkeyes Caitlin 1s in a custom black-and-gold colorway.

Penn improved to 4-3 with the win, while Drexel fell to 3-3. Michael Zanoni led the Quakers with 30 points; David Simonovic scored 20 for the Dragons.

Caitlin Clark also arrives in the offseason after a standout WNBA year : she averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game, finishing second in the league in assists. Her appearance at Penn brought together her basketball career, her signature shoes and a family connection to the team.

articles.title: Nike Caitlin 1 review: Caitlin Clark’s "Cave Stone" shoe gets an on-court test
articles.standfirst: A sneaker creator put Caitlin Clark’s signature shoe through a court test and shared his first impressions
articles.summary: A sneaker creator put Caitlin Clark’s signature shoe through a court test and shared his first impressions
articles.body:
The Nike Caitlin 1 “Cave Stone” made a strong first impression on sneaker creator crosbykicks. In his Instagram review, he rated the shoe’s looks 9/10 and its cushioning 8.25/10. The video also shows him wearing the pair on court and lists its weight at 379 grams, though it doesn’t specify the shoe size.

The short review shows close-ups of the textured upper and outsole, followed by a quick on-court try-on. The creator says the shoe fits true to size. His scores reflect his personal experience wearing the pair, rather than a formal performance assessment.

What to know about Caitlin Clark’s signature shoe

The Caitlin 1 is Clark’s first Nike signature shoe. Nike says it was designed around a quicker first step, a faster step-back and a faster shot release. The line launched globally Oct. 1, with a North American retail price of $140. The Cave Stone colorway is also listed at $140 on Nike’s U.S. site.

Nike lists a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit, a full-length Cushlon midsole and an Opticast upper among the shoe’s features. The Cave Stone colorway uses a muted, light brown-and-stone palette, giving it a more understated look than some of the other Caitlin 1 releases.

Caitlin Clark sets a new pace for Nike’s women’s signature shoes

Nike already had signature shoe lines with Sabrina Ionescu and A’ja Wilson . Ionescu’s Sabrina 1 became one of the most successful signature launches led by a women’s basketball player, while Wilson’s A’One arrived in 2025.

Caitlin Clark’s debut, however, reached a new scale: Nike called the Caitlin 1 its largest women’s signature shoe launch ever, placing it in 5,000 retail locations and reporting strong sell-through. Some launch colorways also sold out quickly online. NIKE, Inc.

That momentum makes the Caitlin 1 feel like part of a new era for women’s signature basketball shoes. Clark has set the pace at every stage of her career from becoming the No. 1 pick in the WNBA draft to reshaping expectations in college basketball and drawing a wider audience to the WNBA.

Now, she is helping set the pace in women’s signature sneakers, this time with Nike.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s “Trainer Barbie” reports for duty as "The Hunting Wives" Season 2 hits Netflix
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star celebrated Thanksgiving by sharing a glimpse of her new role in the Netflix drama
articles.summary: The WNBA star celebrated Thanksgiving by sharing a glimpse of her new role in the Netflix drama
articles.body:
Angel Reese had a new reason to celebrate Thanksgiving: The Hunting Wives Season 2 is now streaming on Netflix, and she’s part of the cast. “Trainer Barbie is reporting for duty,” Reese wrote in an Instagram post, giving fans a look at her character. All eight episodes of the new season are available now.

Reese plays Trainer Barbie, a former athlete who works with Baylor University’s basketball team. Netflix describes her as tough-talking and no-nonsense, with the challenging job of trying to talk some sense into Brad Thompson, a new Baylor player.

From fan of the show to part of its cast

The role brings Reese into the drama of Maple Brook, Texas . The series follows Sophie (Brittany Snow), an East Coast transplant drawn into the wealthy social circle of Margo (Malin Akerman). In Season 2, the two women are at odds, but old secrets and new enemies pull them back into each other’s orbit.

Angel had already made her enthusiasm for the series clear before joining the cast. She publicly expressed interest in being part of its second season; now, she has a role of her own as the show returns. The series marks a major scripted acting credit for the WNBA star.

Her Thanksgiving post turns that career step into a playful introduction: Angel Reese is “Trainer Barbie,” ready to report for duty just as viewers can start watching the new season. It’s a fresh on-screen role for the basketball star and a new reason for her fans to tune in.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark questions Cowboys' decisions with harsh tweet after Thanksgiving collapse
articles.standfirst: Dallas let a promising afternoon slip away in front of its home crowd
articles.summary: Dallas let a promising afternoon slip away in front of its home crowd
articles.body:
The Thanksgiving showdown between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys turned into one of the most dramatic games of the season . What initially looked like a comfortable afternoon for the home team ended in disappointment, with Philadelphia completing a stunning comeback to take a 39-38 victory.

Caitlin Clark reacts as Cowboys suffer heartbreaking defeat

The game took another dramatic turn in the final minutes, when Dallas had an opportunity to protect its lead but failed to convert on fourth-and-one . Instead of extending the drive, Dak Prescott was brought down for a sack, giving Philadelphia possession with a chance to take the lead.

That decision quickly became a talking point among viewers, including WNBA star Caitlin Clark . Following the crucial moment, the Indiana Fever guard took to social media to question what Dallas was trying to accomplish with its late-game decision.

Eagles complete historic comeback against Dallas

Philadelphia capitalized on the opportunity, putting together the drive that eventually allowed Jake Elliott to deliver the winning field goal from 59 yards with just two seconds remaining. The Eagles had erased a 21-point deficit to secure a 39-38 victory, completing one of the most memorable Thanksgiving comebacks in NFL history.

Dallas had been in control for much of the afternoon, building a 31-10 advantage before Philadelphia found its way back into the contest . Joe Milton led the Eagles' comeback, throwing for 331 yards and three touchdowns, while DeVonta Smith finished with 200 receiving yards.

The loss was particularly painful for the Cowboys after having several opportunities to put the game away . Clark's reaction added another voice to the criticism surrounding Dallas' late decisions, as the team watched a victory slip away in the closing seconds.

articles.title: Angel Reese in the spotlight because of what Netflix said after her debut in the streaming world
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese takes her talents to Hollywood as Netflix showcases her new role
articles.summary: Angel Reese takes her talents to Hollywood as Netflix showcases her new role
articles.body:
Angel Reese is taking her talents beyond the basketball court, and Netflix has given fans another reason to talk about her latest venture.

The Atlanta Dream star has made her scripted acting debut in Season 2 of The Hunting Wives, appearing as a character named Trainer Barbie. Netflix has now shared a clip featuring Reese, and there has been no shortage of reaction.

The streaming platform posted a short video from the new season alongside the caption, “Hello Angel Reese in THE HUNTING WIVES Season 2!” The scene features Reese interacting with Baylor basketball recruit Brad Thompson, played by George Ferrier.

Her character helps clean up Brad's bloody nose before delivering some advice to the incoming college player.

Trainer Barbie is a former athlete who works as a basketball trainer at Baylor University. Described as tough-talking and no-nonsense, she's responsible for keeping the confident newcomer under control.

Although Reese is familiar with performing in front of huge crowds, the role represents a different kind of challenge and a new opportunity to showcase her personality.

The casting also has an interesting backstory. Reese had publicly expressed her interest in joining the series in August 2025 after praising it on X. Showrunner Rebecca Cutter responded, prompting the basketball star to ask whether the production needed her for its next season.

Angel Reese's acting debut gets fans talking

Reese celebrated the milestone by sharing her excitement online. Announcing her arrival as Trainer Barbie, she described the character as having a country-chic style with a touch of sex appeal. Her Thanksgiving message also encouraged viewers to mention her when they spotted her in the episodes.

Netflix's announcement wasn't the only thing generating conversation. Fans on social media had different opinions about Reese's performance. While some couldn't wait to see the basketball star on their screens, others questioned her delivery.

"Sounds like she's reading directly from the script," wrote one fan.

The mixed response hasn't taken away from the significance of the opportunity. Reese has already established herself as one of basketball's biggest personalities, and her move into television gives her another platform to connect with audiences.

Her previous screen appearance included a role as herself in A House of Dynamite, making this a notable step into acting.

Her achievements on the court make the crossover even more interesting. During the 2026 WNBA season, the Atlanta forward earned Defensive Player of the Year honours after an impressive campaign.

She collected 521 rebounds, becoming the first player in league history to surpass 500 in a single season. She also established a new single-game record with 26 rebounds and finished with 32 double-doubles.

Meanwhile, The Hunting Wives has plenty more drama ahead. Based on May Cobb's bestselling novel, the series follows Sophie, played by Brittany Snow , as she becomes involved in the privileged and complicated world of Margo, portrayed by Malin Akerman.

Season 2 premiered on November 26, with all 10 episodes available on Netflix. The streaming service has also approved a third season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark shares new reading plans as Rory McIlroy connection sparks interest
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever superstar is turning to a renowned sports psychologist's book as her love for golf continues to influence her offseason plans
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever superstar is turning to a renowned sports psychologist's book as her love for golf continues to influence her offseason plans
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark has revealed an interesting connection behind her next reading choice, with four-time major champion Rory McIlroy playing an unexpected role.

The basketball superstar recently received a copy of Golf Is Not a Game of Perfect, written by renowned sports psychologist Dr. Bob Rotella , and has already earmarked it as her next read.

Speaking to People, Clark explained that McIlroy's professional relationship with Rotella was what initially caught her attention. The Northern Irish golfer has worked with the sports psychologist since 2010, making the book particularly appealing to the 24-year-old basketball star.

“It was written by the sports psychologist Rory McIlroy uses, and I think that’s really fascinating,” Clark said. “I haven’t opened it up yet, but that’s what I’m looking forward to reading next.”

Clark started playing golf at six and currently carries approximately a 15 handicap. She's also participated in several prestigious events, including the PGA Tour's John Deere Classic in 2023 and the LPGA's ANNIKA pro-am in 2024 and 2025.

Those appearances have given her opportunities to play alongside established names such as Nelly Korda and Annika Sörenstam.

Her golfing ambitions haven't stopped there. During an appearance on the New Heights podcast with Jason and Travis Kelce, Clark revealed that playing Augusta National Golf Club for the first time is among her biggest offseason goals.

Caitlin Clark's love of reading leads to personal milestone

Golf isn't the only interest Clark has maintained since childhood. The Indiana Fever guard also developed a strong appreciation for reading, something she credits partly to her mother, who studied English in college and regularly encouraged her children to explore books.

Clark recalled receiving books as Christmas Eve gifts, with each selection accompanied by a handwritten note from her parents. Those childhood experiences helped establish a connection with reading that eventually inspired her own literary project.

Her debut children's picture book, EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams, has already achieved considerable success, reaching No. 1 on the New York Times bestseller list. Inspired by a hand-painted mirror in her childhood bedroom, the story encourages young readers to work hard, remain determined and pursue their biggest ambitions.

Clark also shared that her parents, Brent and Anne , have been particularly proud of the achievement. Her brothers, Blake and Colin , haven't been quite as enthusiastic about reading their sister's work, something she jokingly described as typical sibling behavior.

Away from books and golf, Clark also found herself discussing football during Thanksgiving after watching the Dallas Cowboys suffer a stunning 39-38 defeat against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Dallas surrendered a 21-point advantage, with Clark questioning head coach Brian Schottenheimer's decision to keep the offence on the field during a crucial fourth-and-one situation with 55 seconds remaining.

Clark reacted on X, asking, "What exactly were the Cowboys doing there?"

Dak Prescott was subsequently sacked, giving Philadelphia an opportunity to complete its comeback. Jake Elliott eventually converted a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining.
